lessons.title: 1. The Skeleton
lessons.overview: Learn the hidden structure behind every website on the internet.

content.stepDetail: HTML is like the steel frame of a skyscraper. You don't see it when the building is finished, but without it, the building collapses.
We speak to the browser using Tags. They look like `<tag>Content</tag>`. The first one opens the command, the second one (with the slash `/`) closes it.

quiz.question: Which symbol closes a tag?

consoleExercise.prompt: Write a body tag with the text 'Welcome'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Perfect! You just built the visible part of a webpage.

lessons.title: 2. Headlines (h1-h6)
lessons.overview: Structure your content with titles and subtitles.

content.stepDetail: Newspapers have a big title (H1) and smaller section titles (H2, H3). HTML uses these tags to tell Google what is important.
`<h1>` is the Main Title (use only one). `<h6>` is the smallest subtitle.

quiz.question: Which heading is the most important?
quiz.hint: Number 1 is always the top priority.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create an h1 tag with the text 'My Portfolio'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Great! That will appear as big, bold text.

lessons.title: 3. Paragraphs (p)
lessons.overview: Add blocks of text to your webpage.

content.stepDetail:
You can't just type text loosely. You must wrap it in a `

` tag. This tells the browser 'This is a distinct block of text'.
Browsers automatically add a little empty space (margin) before and after every paragraph to make it readable.

quiz.question: What does 'p' stand for?

consoleExercise.prompt: Write a paragraph that says 'About Me'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Nice. Your text is now structured.

lessons.title: 4. Bold & Italics
lessons.overview: Emphasize specific words for impact.

content.stepDetail: `<b>` makes text bold, but `<strong>` tells screen readers the text is IMPORTANT.
Similarly, `<i>` creates visual italics, while `<em>` adds semantic emphasis to the tone.

quiz.question: Which tag indicates importance?
quiz.hint: It adds strength to the meaning.

consoleExercise.prompt: Make the word 'Warning' important using strong.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Strong work! Accessibility matters.

lessons.title: 5. Links (Anchor Tags)
lessons.overview: Connect your page to the rest of the world.

content.stepDetail: Links are the 'Web' in 'World Wide Web'. The `<a>` tag stands for Anchor. It anchors your page to another page.
The `href` attribute tells the browser where to go. Think of it as the destination address on an envelope.

quiz.question: Which attribute holds the URL?

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a link to 'site.com' with text 'Go'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: You just built a bridge to another website!

lessons.title: 6. Images (img)
lessons.overview: Add visual content to your site.

content.stepDetail: Images don't wrap text, so they don't need a closing tag. They just sit there. We write them as ``.
`src` tells the browser which file to load. If the filename is wrong, you get a broken icon.

quiz.question: Does have a closing tag?

consoleExercise.prompt: Add an image with source 'logo.png'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Looks good! Visuals make sites engaging.

lessons.title: 7. Lists (ul & ol)
lessons.overview: Organize items into bullet points or numbered steps.

content.stepDetail: Use `<ul>` (Unordered List) for bullet points where order doesn't matter (like groceries).
Use `<ol>` (Ordered List) for numbered steps where order matters (1. Mix, 2. Bake).

quiz.question: Which tag creates a bulleted list?

consoleExercise.prompt: Create an unordered list with one item 'Apple'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Organized! Lists are used everywhere.

lessons.title: 8. Attributes (ID & Class)
lessons.overview: Give your elements unique names and group labels.

content.stepDetail: An `id` is unique. Only one element on the page can have `id='main-title'`. Use it for specific landmarks.
A `class` is for groups. Many elements can have `class='button'`. They all join the 'button' team and look the same.

quiz.question: Can two elements share the same ID?
quiz.hint: IDs must be unique, like a passport number.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a div with the class 'container'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Correct! Classes allow you to style many items at once.

lessons.title: 9. Containers (div & span)
lessons.overview: Group elements together for layout and styling.

content.stepDetail: `<div>` defines a Division. It's an empty box. We use it to group things together (like a sidebar or a card).
`<span>` is used to grab a small piece of text inside a line, usually to color it or make it bold.

quiz.question: Which tag is best for grouping large sections?

consoleExercise.prompt: Wrap the text 'Hello' inside a span.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Precision! Spans are great for styling specific words.

lessons.title: 10. Forms (Input)
lessons.overview: Collect data from your users.

content.stepDetail: The `<input>` tag changes shape based on its `type`. It can be a text box, a checkbox, or a password field.
`placeholder` is the grey text inside the box that gives the user a hint (e.g., 'Enter email here').

quiz.question: How do you make a password field?
quiz.hint: It hides the characters as dots.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create an input with type 'email'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: User ready! This will open the email keyboard on phones.

lessons.title: 11. Advanced Input
lessons.overview: Checkboxes, Radios, and Dropdowns.

content.stepDetail: Use `checkbox` for multiple options. Use `radio` for single choice (like Gender). Use `<select>` for a dropdown menu.

quiz.question: Which input allows multiple selections?
quiz.hint: You can check more than one box.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create an input with type 'checkbox'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Interactive forms are powerful.

lessons.title: 12. Text Area & Labels
lessons.overview: Collecting long messages and labeling inputs.

content.stepDetail: For comments or bios, use `<textarea>`. Unlike `<input>`, it has a closing tag.
Wrapping text in a `<label>` makes it clickable, which helps focus the input box.

quiz.question: Which tag is best for a long comment?

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a textarea element.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Now users can write essays!

lessons.title: 13. Tables
lessons.overview: Display data in rows and columns.

content.stepDetail: Tables are built row by row. First `<table>` opens the sheet. Then `<tr>` opens a Table Row.
Inside a row, we use `<td>` (Table Data) for the actual cell content.

quiz.question: What does <tr> stand for?
quiz.hint: It creates a horizontal line of cells.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a row (tr) with one cell (td) saying 'Hi'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: You're thinking like a database now.

lessons.title: 14. Buttons & Actions
lessons.overview: Make clickable elements to submit forms or trigger scripts.

content.stepDetail: Buttons are the main way users say 'Go'. They can submit forms or run JavaScript code.
Use Links (`<a>`) to go to a new page. Use Buttons (`<button>`) to perform an action on the *current* page.

quiz.question: When should you use a <button>?
quiz.hint: Links go places; Buttons do things.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a button with text 'Login'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Clickable! This is essential for interactivity.

lessons.title: 15. Semantic HTML
lessons.overview: Write meaningful code that machines can understand.

content.stepDetail: Instead of using `<div>` for everything, use specific tags. Use `<header>` for the top, `<footer>` for the bottom.
It helps Screen Readers (for blind users) navigate your site and helps Google understand your content structure.

quiz.question: Where should copyright info go?
quiz.hint: It belongs at the bottom of the page.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a footer tag containing 'Copyright'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Professional touch! Semantics matter for accessibility.

lessons.title: 16. Multimedia
lessons.overview: Embed sound and video directly into your page.

content.stepDetail: HTML5 allows you to play files without plugins. Just point the `src` to your file.
Don't forget the `controls` attribute! Without it, the user can't play, pause, or change volume.

quiz.question: What attribute adds the play/pause buttons?

consoleExercise.prompt: Add an audio tag with 'controls'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Sound check passed!

lessons.title: 17. Metadata (Head)
lessons.overview: Information about your page that users don't see.

content.stepDetail: The `<body>` is what users see. The `<head>` is what Google and the Browser see. It holds settings.
The `<title>` tag sets the name you see on the browser tab or in search results.

quiz.question: Where does the <title> tag go?

consoleExercise.prompt: Set the title to 'Home'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Correct! That's what shows up in Google Search.

lessons.title: 18. SEO Basics
lessons.overview: Helping Google find your website.

content.stepDetail: SEO is how you rank higher on Google. The `description` meta tag is the snippet of text people see under your link in search results.

quiz.question: Where is the meta description placed?

consoleExercise.prompt: Write a meta tag with name='description'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: You're now visible to search engines!

lessons.title: 19. Favicons & Icons
lessons.overview: Adding the tiny icon to the browser tab.

content.stepDetail: A Favicon is the tiny logo in the browser tab. We use the `<link>` tag inside the head to set it.

quiz.question: What is the relationship (rel) for a favicon?

consoleExercise.prompt: Link an icon with href='logo.ico'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Polished! Your site looks professional.

lessons.title: 20. Project: Portfolio
lessons.overview: Combine everything to build a personal profile structure.

content.stepDetail: You need a Header (Name), Main (About text + Image), and Footer (Contact Link).

Remember: Tags go inside tags. The `` goes inside the `
`, which goes inside the ``.

quiz.question: Which tag holds all the visible content?
quiz.hint: It's the body of the document.

consoleExercise.prompt: Create a main tag containing an h1 'Profile'.
consoleExercise.successMessage: Congratulations! You are now an HTML Architect.
